newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: U.S. politician meets Nicaraguan drug trafficker.
newsitem.headline: U.S. politician meets Nicaraguan drug trafficker.

text.p: A U.S. congresswoman said a jailed Nicaraguan drug trafficker should be questioned by U.S. authorities investigating charges the CIA allowed cocaine sales to finance right-wing Nicaraguan rebels in the 1980s.
Representative Maxine Waters, a California Democrat, told reporters on Friday during a five-hour visit to Nicaragua that she had met with imprisoned drug trafficker Enrique Miranda.

"He was able to share with me that he does indeed have knowledge of the drug trafficking operation ... as it operated in the Los Angeles area," said Waters, who represents an inner-city Los Angeles neighbourhood hard-hit by crack cocaine.
"He has told me enough to be able to advise our investigators that they should follow it up," she said.

Allegations that a drug ring flooded Los Angeles ghettos with crack cocaine and funnelled profits to U.S.-backed Contra rebels in Nicaragua were made in August 1996 in a three-part investigative series published in the San Jose Mercury News.
The newspaper said the ring was headed by two Nicaraguans, Danilo Blandon and Norwin Meneses. Meneses is currently in prison in Nicaragua on drug trafficking charges.
The newspaper said the drug pipeline between Colombia and California, passing through Nicaragua, operated for 10 years with at least tacit CIA approval.
The case sent shock waves through black communities devastated by the crack epidemic and led the CIA and Justice Departments to open investigations into the case.

Miranda, in prison on drug trafficking charges, is an associate of Meneses and Blandon and was arrested along with Meneses in 1991 for trying to smuggle 1,653 lbs (750 kg) of cocaine into the United States.

Sentenced to seven years in prison, Miranda, a former Sandinista intelligence official, fled Nicaragua in 1995 while on a pass from prison and went to the United States. But he was arrested by the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation on Dec. 2, 1996, and extradited to Nicaragua the next day.
